name: Fraxinus excelsior extract
description: Fraxinus excelsior extract (CAS 84625-28-5 ), derived from the common ash tree, is a botanical active used in personal care and pharmaceutical formulations for its antioxidant and moisture-retention properties. Commercially sourced as a standardized plant extract, it delivers functional performance in skin-conditioning and protective applications. In cosmetic formulations, it is incorporated into serums, creams, and lotions. It is utilized where antioxidant stabilization of the formula and support for skin hydration are both required from a single botanical ingredient. Anti-aging and moisturizing skincare lines use it to address oxidative stress. This extract helps maintain a natural-origin ingredient profile at the formulation level. Pharmaceutical and nutraceutical product developers source it for topical preparations where plant-derived humectant activity is a requirement. It also appears in hair care products targeting scalp conditioning, where its moisture-binding capacity supports leave-on and rinse-off formats. The extract is supplied as a liquid, dry powder, or glycolic solution. Cosmetic-grade and standardized botanical extract specifications are the most common commercial forms available from ingredient suppliers. Buyers should confirm standardization markers and solvent systems with their sources. These specifications vary across production sources and intended application formats. Ensuring the extract meets necessary quality benchmarks is essential for maintaining consistency in high-performance personal care products.
